listing.name: Banjo-Tooie / Banjo-Tooie: Recompiled (Vidanox)
listing.summary: Use the Banjo-Tooie player package and select your own USA cartridge dump.

steps.title: Choose your original cartridge dump on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then Select ROM and supply your own Banjo-Tooie USA 32 MiB cartridge dump. The project recommends an unmodified big-endian .z64; the player also converts byteswapped dumps of the same cartridge. Another region or a modified image is not accepted. The player checks the file and keeps its own copy in its profile, so keep your original separately.

steps.title: Keep the complete player package
steps.instruction: For a copy you manage yourself, extract the whole package. On Windows, run BanjoTooieRecompiled.exe with assets and the supplied SDL2 and DXC libraries beside it. On Linux, run run.sh, or start BanjoTooieRecompiled with its extracted folder as the working folder.

warnings: Upstream calls Linux less exercised than Windows. Portcove has not observed native setup, gameplay or saves. On Linux the player needs Vulkan, SDL2, FreeType, D-Bus and a running xdg-desktop-portal service for Select ROM.

The package includes the Suplexmentary Comic NC font, which the project license does not cover, and menu art based on Rare's promotional artwork. Portcove downloads the package only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.

references.title: Keep your actual profile when updating
references.instruction: Preserve the player's profile before replacing a copy you manage yourself: normally %LOCALAPPDATA%\BanjoTooieRecompiled on Windows or ~/.config/BanjoTooieRecompiled on Linux. It holds the copied original bt.n64.us.1.0.z64, saves, settings and mods. For Flatpak, keep the complete ~/.var/app/io.github.Vidanox.BanjoTooieRecompiled folder, and keep any APP_FOLDER_PATH or portable.txt folder you actually used. Keep a working copy before replacing the player.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, choose Select ROM and pick your own Banjo-Tooie USA cartridge dump. The player checks it and keeps a copy named bt.n64.us.1.0.z64 in its profile, together with saves, settings and mods; keep your original separately. The profile is %LOCALAPPDATA%\BanjoTooieRecompiled on Windows and ~/.config/BanjoTooieRecompiled on Linux. Portcove starts the managed copy without APP_FOLDER_PATH, so a copy you run with APP_FOLDER_PATH keeps a separate profile; a copy you manage yourself without portable.txt or APP_FOLDER_PATH shares the managed profile. Portcove refuses to start a managed copy that contains portable.txt. Portcove neither backs up nor removes the profile, and rollback does not rewind it; back it up before changing versions. On Linux the player needs Vulkan, SDL2, FreeType, D-Bus and a running xdg-desktop-portal service. Portcove replaces the player; you own the original and the profile.
